name: Ascend custom (PLACEHOLDER: values inherited from 910B)
_comment_clock: MEASURED. msprof reports Current Freq: 1650 and Rated Freq: 1650 on this part. The 1.85 inherited from 910B made every microsecond figure 12% optimistic while leaving cycle counts untouched, so it hid rather than showed. cycles_per_us is not parsed -- the loader derives it from frequency_ghz -- and is kept only so the two do not disagree on paper.

ub.description: MEASURED capacity. The binary compiler names it when a kernel overruns: 'ub overflow, requires 2764800 bits while 2031616 bits available'. 2031616 bits is 253952 bytes, i.e. 248 KB, against the 192 KB inherited here from another part. Nothing in the estimate divides by this -- it is reported next to what the module allocates, because that is the constraint that decides whether a block partition can be compiled at all.

fixpipe_ub.description: Cube output: L0C to UB, staying on chip instead of going out to HBM and back. PLACEHOLDER bandwidth.

ub_to_l1.description: On-chip Vector-to-Cube staging: UB to L1, avoiding the HBM round trip. Reported as unit mte3_ub_l1 and modelled as a mover of its own, so it overlaps off-chip mte3 traffic: UB can drain to L1 and stream to L2 at the same time. PLACEHOLDER bandwidth.

l1_to_ub.description: On-chip Cube-to-Vector staging: L1 to UB. Reported as unit mte1_l1_ub and modelled as a mover of its own, so it overlaps off-chip vec_mte2 traffic. PLACEHOLDER bandwidth.

cube_path.description: Matrix multiplication data flow; on this target the result may drain to UB instead of HBM

inter_path.description: Cube and Vector paths execute in parallel

intra_path.description: All units within each path can execute in parallel (pipelined)

calibration.description: Parameters calibrated from _attn_fwd (flash attention) profiling on Ascend 910B. Input: Z=1,H=8,N_CTX=192,HEAD_DIM=128. BLOCK_M in {16,32,48,64}, BLOCK_N=64 fixed. Hardware: Block Dim=20 (AIC) + 20 AIV = Mix Block Dim 40.

startup_latencies.notes: vector: was 10, increased to reflect UB read-after-write stall in serial dependency chains (sub->exp->reduce). mte2: restored to 50 (actual DMA startup); pipe_barrier overhead now modeled separately in estimateDuration.

vector_op_cycles_per_vec_instruction.notes: Calibrated ordering for vector ALU ops: vadd/vsub/vmul remain the cheapest, vreduce is only slightly heavier, and vexp is typically about 4x the cost of simple arithmetic. Other transcendental and divide-like ops stay between those extremes.

scalar_overhead.description: aiv_vec_ratio converges to 0.211 for BM>=48. Total AIV time = vec_time * (1/0.211) = vec_time * 4.74, equivalently vec_time * (1 + 3.74). Scalar fraction covers loop control, pointer arithmetic, and pipe_barrier sync between AIC and AIV. Completely absent from prior model.

parallelism.description: From profiling: Block Dim=20, Mix Block Dim=40 (2 AIV per AIC block).

pipe_barrier.description: Calibrated from BM=64 (1 AIV wave, 24 programs). AIV wall time=31.993us=59187 cycles. Active fraction (vec+scalar+mte) sums to 61.1%, leaving 38.9% idle=23044 cycles. With N_iter=3 inner iterations per program: 23044/3 ~ 7500 cycles per pipe_barrier.

wave_overhead.description: Observed aiv_time decreases monotonically with fewer AIV waves: BM=16(3 waves)->BM=32(2 waves)->BM=48(1 wave). BM=64 also 1 wave but with lower program count, making BM=48 and BM=64 near-equal (exception to the monotonic trend). The wave count multiplier N_waves=ceil(N_programs/N_AIV) is applied to per-program cycles to produce kernel-level time.

tilesim.description: Knobs for the tilesim-migrated micro-architecture model (root cause 1/2).

small_packet.description: Global small-packet bandwidth fitting coefficients (tilesim 910B1.yaml pkt_param). Applied to EVERY mover when enable_small_packet_bw is on, mirroring tilesim's single global pkt_param dict; a per-table bandwidth_tables[*].small_packet entry overrides these. Bucket selection: <64B -> 64B, <128B -> 128B, <256B -> 256B; formula bw = b/(a*b + pktBytes/(1024^3)).

mutex_groups.description: Hardware units that share a physical pipeline and cannot execute in parallel (tilesim MutexComponents / pipe_exclusive_config). Each clique is an array of costmodel unit names (cube/cube_mte2/fixpipe/fixpipe_ub/vector/vec_mte2/mte3/mte3_ub_l1/mte1_l1_ub/scalar). 910B: AIV MTE2 (vec load) and MTE3 (vec store) share one pipeline -> they serialize, so the vector-path roofline uses max(vector, vec_mte2 + mte3) instead of max(vector, vec_mte2, mte3). UNVERIFIED for this target, and all three of these are answered by adding a clique here rather than by changing code: (1) the vec_mte2/mte3 clique is inherited from 910B; (2) whether fixpipe and fixpipe_ub share one physical pipe -- if so add ["fixpipe", "fixpipe_ub"]; (3) the on-chip movers mte3_ub_l1 and mte1_l1_ub are modelled as independent of each other and of the off-chip ones, so UB can drain to L1 while streaming to L2 -- if any of those pairs really shares a pipe, add it as a clique.

synchronisation.description: Fixed cost of crossing one synchronisation barrier: the flag write, its propagation, and the wait that observes it. Charged as latency in the block schedule, not as pipe occupancy, because a barrier stops the core from issuing rather than keeping an engine busy -- so it can only ever show up through the recurrence bound, never through the resource bound. UNMEASURED on this target: 0 means the barrier is treated as free, which is what the model did before this field existed. Set it before comparing IR variants that differ in HOW MANY barriers they contain (a finer block partition adds barriers), because at 0 splitting a compute block in two is free and a search over partitions has a degenerate optimum at one operation per block.

vector_datapath.description: MEASURED. Bytes one vector core consumes per cycle. vec_cycle_tables was migrated from a part whose datapath is 128 B/cycle -- a 256-byte repeat at compute=2 -- and its numbers are rescaled by the ratio rather than edited, so the relative cost between intrinsics is preserved. Derived by least squares over three tile configurations spanning 3.1x in total repeats, which gave 0.89 cycles per repeat and, independently and without being fitted, 35.8 cycles of per-instruction startup against the 35 already in the model. That second agreement is what says the formula's shape is right and only this one number was wrong. 0.89 cycles per 256-byte repeat is 288 B/cycle; 256 is the physically natural value next to it and is what is set here, leaving the model about 6% over on the compute term.

scalar_issue.description: UNMEASURED, and left at zero for that reason. Each core's scalar unit runs address arithmetic, loop bookkeeping and predicate evaluation; the profiler puts that at 19-24% of the Cube's active time and 14-20% of the Vector's, and -- the part that matters for choosing a block partition -- at 232, 239 and 252 cycles per iteration across three tile configurations whose area differs fourfold. It scales with blocks, not with data. What is missing is the split between per-instruction and per-block: every run so far had eleven blocks, so the two cannot be told apart. The estimate report prints the weighted instruction count next to this, which is the other half of the division; one profiled run fills it in.

core_pairing.description: MEASURED. How many vector cores execute one compute block's vector work. The runtime reports 28 cube cores and 56 vector cores, msprof prints two vector sub-block rows against every cube row, and the two rows carry the SAME instruction count -- 152 166 MTE3 instructions each on flash attention, against the 152 165 this model derives for a single core -- while the block's tile is only moved once. That is a split of the data, not of the instruction stream, so a repeat count is halved and a startup latency is not. Only the vector arithmetic uses this: the transfer engines are charged from bandwidths that were themselves read off a running sub-core, so they already contain the split and must not be divided again.

bandwidth_tables.description: Per-(src:dst[,corenum,pkt]) bandwidth in GB/s, migrated from tilesim bandwidth_910B1.csv (GM->hbm, SHM->l2). Costmodel space names: hbm/l2/l1/l0a/l0b/l0c/ub. Core-dependent movers carry per_core_gbps (1..48); others use bandwidth_gbps. This target adds l0c:ub, ub:l1 and l1:ub. Their values here are PLACEHOLDERS copied from comparable 910B paths (l0c:l1 and l2:ub) and must be replaced with measurements.
bandwidth_tables._comment_l0c_ub: MEASURED, not a placeholder any more. msprof reports aic_fixpipe_active_bw = 244.9 GB/s on flash attention, read straight off the engine rather than inferred from its occupancy. The inherited 70 GB/s made the Cube drain look three to four times slower than the matmul that fed it, which is backwards for a path that exists to keep the result on chip.
bandwidth_tables._comment_l1_l0: MEASURED. Staging the Cube's operands from L1 into L0A/L0B, which the profiler reports as aic_mte1_time and which nothing in the model charged until the matmul started paying for it. msprof gives aic_mte1_active_bw between 292 and 361 GB/s across configurations, and the arithmetic agrees from the other side: four instructions per inner iteration moving 128 KB in about 560 cycles is ~234 B/cycle, i.e. ~386 GB/s. 355 sits inside that range. Worth a direct microbenchmark: the figure comes from one kernel's occupancy and inherits whatever else that occupancy contains.

vec_cycle_tables.description: Per-(intrinsic,dtype) vector cycle triplets {compute,head,interval}, migrated from tilesim vec_cycle_910B1.csv. dtype keys fp16 (covers fp16/bf16) and fp32. cycles = compute * repeats + startup, repeats = ceil(numElems*elemBytes/256).

status: DRAFT. The topology below is the newer one -- the Cube accumulator can drain straight into UB, and UB and L1 talk to each other on chip -- but every bandwidth, latency and cycle figure is still the measured 910B value. Replace them with measurements before trusting any absolute number from this profile. Until then it is useful for checking that the new data paths are picked up, not for predicting time.
